glossary.flow: One evidence-backed path from an entry point toward a meaningful boundary.
glossary.trigger: The API route, CLI command, or queue message that starts work.
glossary.API: An application programming interface exposed for another program to call.
glossary.OData: A standard for querying and changing data through HTTP APIs.
glossary.cli: A command-line command registered by the application.
glossary.handler: The first function or method directly bound to a trigger.
glossary.call: A direct source-code call whose target was resolved heuristically.
glossary.database: A call that appears to cross into persistent storage; traversal stops here.
glossary.external: A call that appears to leave the process over a network client; traversal stops here.
glossary.queue: A publish or enqueue call; downstream processing is a separate flow.
glossary.tenant: A customer or organizational boundary whose data and configuration are isolated.
glossary.adapter: Code that translates between an application-facing interface and an external technology.
glossary.provider: A component that supplies data or operations behind an interface.
glossary.port: An application-owned interface through which core logic communicates with adapters.
glossary.entity provider: A provider that loads or stores domain entities, often through a search or database system.
glossary.OpenSearch: A search and document-storage engine; named only when matching source or type evidence exists.
glossary.IoT thing: A cloud representation of a physical or logical Internet of Things device.
glossary.Greengrass: AWS edge software used to deploy and run workloads near IoT devices.
glossary.SQS: Amazon Simple Queue Service, used for asynchronous message delivery.
glossary.EventBridge: An AWS event bus used to route events between producers and consumers.
glossary.MQTT: A lightweight publish/subscribe protocol commonly used by IoT devices.
glossary.SPOF: Single point of failure: one component whose loss can stop a larger workflow.
glossary.confidence: High means direct binding or unique typed resolution; medium means a conservative naming heuristic.
glossary.evidence: The concrete source relationship supporting a step. It is not runtime proof.
glossary.warning: A place where evidence was insufficient or an output safety limit was reached.
